# Run: How to fix short curbs

<!-- Generated by the `council` CLI. Editable by hand. -->

## Thesis

A parking curb at an airport is vital for congestion. B&A airport has a remarkably short congested parking curb of 500 ft, and they want to make it better. Do some research on how to make it better.

## Audience

Airport executives, capital planners, and policy readers. Assume sophistication, skepticism, and that they have read McKinsey decks and are tired of them.

## Tone

Analytical sharp. Direct. Evidence-dense. Intellectually honest about the counter-argument. Slightly provocative but not polemical. Model: Matt Levine on aviation, not a consultant thought-leadership piece.

## Length

4,000–6,000 words for the full research report; ~1,100-word executive summary.

## Output format

report

## What this is NOT

- Avoid architecture diagrams.

## What this IS

- I'd say what's in scope is anything related to an airport.
- A sharp, evidence-driven argument that earns its conclusions

## Success criteria

- I'd say what's in scope is anything related to an airport.
